text:
maria: hey team — running into a weird one when trying to get our sampleapp onboarding flow working on the edge runtime. built with Vite (esbuild) + TS, depends on the JS SDK which ships both ESM + CJS. app works locally (node) but fails on deploy with a module resolution error. anyone seen this? :confused:

ash: can you paste the error? also which bundler + target?

maria: deploy log snippet:
```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
 at internalCompile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:999:18)
 at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1033:13)
 at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1103:10)
```
this only happens when the edge runtime is selected (CloudEdge). local dev server (vite) + node target is fine. package.json of sampleapp has "type": "module" and we import the SDK like `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';`

jonathan: hmm. sounds like a hybrid ESM/CJS package is being emitted and the edge loader is choking on a CJS entrypoint. do you have `exports` or `main`/`module` fields in node package? some bundlers will prefer `main` (cjs) if exports mapping isn't present.

maria: SDK package.json (from node_modules):
```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/inference",
  "version": "1.6.2",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}
```

samira: aha — exports only exposes package.json. so bundlers that support exports mapping will pick module/main heuristics differently. Vite/esbuild on edge seems to try to load the CJS `main` and runtime treats it as ESM which yields that error. we had a similar issue in a couple customer sample apps.

ash: short repro steps that worked for me locally:
1) `npx degit repo/sampleapp tmp`
2) in tmp: `npm i` (pulls @redwood/inference)
3) `vite build --ssr` with `target=es2022` and `ssr` entry to the server bundle
4) run `node dist/server/entry.js` -> fails with the same stack

jonathan: workaround options:
- SDK: add full exports map so `import` can resolve to `dist/index.esm.js` for modern fields (e.g., `"./": { "import": "./dist/index.esm.js", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js" }`).
- App: add bundler alias in vite config: `resolve.alias: { '@redwood/inference': '/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.esm.js' }` (hacky but works for onboarding/sampleapps)
- Packagers: set `package.json` "type" to "commonjs" or ensure build emits only ESM for edge-targeted bundles.

maria: thanks — the alias trick worked for me as a stopgap. is changing exports in the SDK a breaking change?

samira: it's not breaking if you keep both import/require keys. we should add an exports map and also ship a `exports` fallback for package.json. small PR on the SDK repo should do it. also add a test that runs a vite+esbuild SSR build against the package to catch regressions.

jonathan: also watch out for types: TS users import types from the package root. if we change exports, some consumers may need `types` path re-exported. include `types` in exports: `{ "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }` or add `"typesVersions"` entry.

maria: I opened an issue and attached a tiny repro. i'll try to draft a PR for the exports map. thanks for quick ideas. :pray:

deploy-bot: build #4821 failed on preview-edge for sampleapp-onboard (logs: https://ci.redwood/4821).

ash: once PR is up ping me. i'll try to add a CI job in the SDK repo that runs a Vite SSR smoke test (edge target). should catch this earlier during releases.

maria: will do. logging this as part of the onboarding friction epic — note: doc suggestion for sampleapp README: "If you're deploying to Edge runtimes, prefer ESM entrypoints or add a resolve alias in Vite."

jonathan: +1. also add a short note about `exports` to the SDK migration docs.

samira: fyi i found a related typing quirk: when you alias to the ESM file, TS sometimes can't find types unless `types` is an explicit entry in `exports`. so include that in the PR too.

maria: perfect. i'll loop in docs + QA once PR is ready. thanks all! :tada:
